newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Karachi power utility sacks 240 workers.
newsitem.headline: Karachi power utility sacks 240 workers.

text.p: Pakistan's Karachi Electric Power Supply Corporation has sacked 240 workers to cut its expenses and plans a further reduction in the coming months, a KESC spokesman said on Thursday.

"Services of 240 employees including 39 officers have been terminated this month to re-organise and re-structure the department which is faced with acute financial problem," the spokesman told Reuters.
But he gave no details the exact number of employees the corporation plans to sack and the amount to be saved by slashing administrative expenses.
The services of 39 officers including engineers were terminated on Wednesday, while 201 lower grade employees were sacked early this month.

KESC, a power generation, transmission and distribution company, announced a first-half loss of 2.286 billion rupees ($57 million) in 1996/97 (July-June) against a profit of 654 million rupees in the same period of 1995/96.

The rising fuel costs and transmission and distribution losses were described as the key reasons for the declining fortunes of the corportaion by KESC's Managing Director Malik Shahid Hamid in an interview to Reuters last week.
The KESC's administrative costs account for about 13 percent of total expenses, against the 86 percent expenses including fuel costs, debt repayments and depreciation.
The Collective Bargaining Agent of the KESC employees has said it would resist laying-off of workers and challenge the decision in the court.

"We are already under-staffed. Services of those employees have been sacked who were recruited during the former Benazir Bhutto government which is political victimisation," said labour leader Akhlaq Khan.
The 10-rupee share of KESC rose 0.25 rupees to 17.25 at the Karachi Stock Exchange at close on Thursday.
